findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:~291 — The `.cooked .signature ... a` (name link) rule was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`. The light-theme lightness silently changed from 30% to 70%, unintentionally making the text much lighter in light themes. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` to preserve the original light appearance.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:~522 — The `.user-profile .names .name` rule changed from `$lightness: 30%` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. The light-theme value was altered (30% → 50%) as a side effect of adding dark-theme support, changing the rendered color for all existing light themes. Should keep 30% for the light variant.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:~497 — The mobile `.names .name` rule changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, unintentionally changing the light-theme color.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:~180 — The `.topic-map h3` (or adjacent h3) rule changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. Light-theme lightness changed 20% → 50%, noticeably lightening headings in light themes. The light variant should stay at 20% (dark variant 80%) to match the equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss:~321, which correctly uses 20%/80%).

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:~101 — `.custom-message-length` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), ...)`. The light-theme value was flipped from 70% to 30% (dark text on light background instead of light gray hint text), inconsistent with the parallel desktop change in desktop/modal.scss:~49 which correctly uses 70% light / 30% dark. Mobile hint text will now render much darker than desktop for the same modal.

The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` near the shown hunk (~288), the `a { ... color: ... }` rule is changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This verifiably changes the light-theme color from a 30% lightness variant to a much lighter 70% variant, while many other conversions in the diff keep the original `$primary` lightness for the light-theme branch and adjust `$secondary` for dark-theme. That makes the finding's claim (unintentional light-theme brightening; should likely be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`) grounded in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss`, the `.names .name` color is indeed changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which alters the light-theme value from a 30% lightness scale to a 50% lightness scale. However, the diff provides no indication this is unintended or incorrect—this PR broadly replaces many `scale-color($primary, ...)` usages with `dark-light-choose(...)`—so it's a legitimate, specific review concern about a visual change rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, the `a.star h3` rule changes from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, which does alter the light-theme value from 20% to 50% (lighter). In the same PR, the analogous desktop rule keeps the 20% light-theme intent by using `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff and would likely cause an unintended mobile heading color regression in light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:~101 — `.custom-message-length` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), ...)`. The light-theme value was flipped from 70% to 30% (dark text on light background instead of light gray hint text), inconsistent with the parallel desktop change in desktop/modal.scss:~49 which correctly uses 70% light / 30% dark. Mobile hint text will now render much darker than desktop for the same modal.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` changes `.custom-message-length` from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`, which indeed flips the light-theme value from 70% to 30%. In contrast, `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss` changes the analogous hint styling to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, keeping 70% for light theme and 30% for dark theme. This diff-grounded mismatch would make the mobile hint text much darker in light mode than desktop, indicating a likely visual regression/defect.
